subproblem.title: First variation of a general varifold: mass derivative (8.2.2–2.4) and representation (8.2.5–2.10)
subproblem.statement: For all N, n, open U ⊆ ℝ^N and n-varifolds V on U: (a) (Simon 8.2.2–8.2.4) if K ⊆ U is compact, φ : ℝ × ℝ^N → ℝ^N is C² on (−1,1) × U with φ(0,x) = x on U, each φ_t := φ(t,·) (|t| < 1) maps U injectively into U and equals the identity on U ∖ K, and X(x) is the t-derivative of φ(t,x) at t = 0 for x ∈ U, then t ↦ (V.pushforwardMeasure φ_t (K × G(N,n))).toReal = M(φ_{t#}V ⌞ Gₙ(K)) has derivative δV(X) = ∫ div_S X dV at t = 0; and div_S X(x) = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DX(x)τ_i⟩ for every S ∈ G(N,n) and orthonormal basis τ of S. (b) (Simon 8.2.5–8.2.10) if V has locally bounded first variation, then variationMeasure V is the measure ‖δV‖ characterised by 2.5; for μ_V-a.e. x, variationDensity V x = D_{μ_V}‖δV‖(x) is finite and is the limit of ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x))/μ_V(B_ρ(x)) as ρ ↓ 0; μ_V(generalizedBoundary V) = 0; and there is a Borel ν : ℝ^N → ℝ^N with |ν| = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e. such that for every X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N): ⟨ν,X⟩ is ‖δV‖-integrable and δV(X) = −∫⟨ν,X⟩ d‖δV‖, ⟨H,X⟩ is μ_V-integrable and ⟨ν,X⟩ is σ-integrable, and δV(X) = −∫⟨H,X⟩ dμ_V − ∫⟨ν,X⟩ dσ, where H = generalizedMeanCurvature V ν and σ = generalizedBoundaryMeasure V. (Exactly FirstVariationIsMassDerivative ∧ FirstVariationRepresentation.)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, §2 (2.1–2.10), printed pp. 208–210; the computation “exactly as in §5 of Ch. 2” and the Riesz/differentiation theorems of Ch. 1 (4.14, 3.23, 3.24) that the book cites. No erratum affects 2.1–2.10. Correction relative to an earlier draft of this proof: under the hypothesis that φ is only C² one may NOT claim D_xφ_t = I + t·DX + O(t²) uniformly (a C² family can have a remainder of exact order |t|^{3/2} at a point, e.g. via g(x+t) − g(x) with g(u) = |u|^{5/2}); the argument below uses only continuity of ∂_tD_xφ, i.e. a uniform o(t) remainder, and differentiates the Jacobian on a short time interval where it is bounded away from 0. Notation: G = Grassmannian N n (orthogonal projection matrices; P_S := S.1 is the projection matrix of S ∈ G), Gₙ(A) = A × G, μ_V = V.weight, ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V, closed balls B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, K(U;ℝ^N) = Varifold.TestVectorField U.

PART (a): FirstVariationIsMassDerivative (2.2–2.4).

1. Setup (2.1). Fix N, n, U, V, φ, K, X as in the hypotheses: K ⊆ U compact, φ is C² on (−1,1) × U, φ(0,·) = id on U, for t ∈ (−1,1) the map φ_t := φ(t,·) maps U into U and is injective on U, φ_t = id on U ∖ K, and HasDerivAt (t ↦ φ(t,x)) (X x) 0 for x ∈ U. (U is open: V.isOpen_domain.) By 2.1 the image varifold is φ_{t#}V(A) = ∫_{F_t⁻¹(A)} J_Sφ_t(x) dV(x,S), F_t(x,S) = (φ_t(x), dφ_t(x)(S)), J_Sφ_t = (det((dφ_t|S)*(dφ_t|S)))^{1/2}; in the contract this is V.pushforwardMeasure (fun x ↦ φ (t, x)) = (imageMap φ_t)_#(J·V) (Varifold.pushforwardMeasure, with imageMap φ_t (x,S) = (φ_t x, transportedPlane φ_t x S)). Only the first component of imageMap φ_t enters the evaluation on the cylinder K × G below, but since the push-forward is a Measure.map, its evaluation formula requires (a.e.-)measurability of the whole map imageMap φ_t; this holds because φ_t is C¹ on U (SimonGMT Varifold.aemeasurable_imageMap / measurable_imageMap_domain, which give the evaluation formula Varifold.pushforwardMeasure_apply_of_contDiffOn).

2. φ_t(K) ⊆ K and U ∩ φ_t⁻¹(K) = K. If x ∈ U ∖ K then φ_t(x) = x ∉ K. If x ∈ K and u := φ_t(x) ∉ K, then u ∈ U ∖ K, so φ_t(u) = u = φ_t(x) and injectivity on U gives x = u ∉ K, a contradiction. Since V is carried by U × G (V.supported) and imageMap φ_t⁻¹(K × G) = φ_t⁻¹(K) × G, which agrees with K × G up to the V-null set Uᶜ × G, the evaluation formula gives (SimonGMT imageMap_preimage_cylinder_ae_of_fixed and pushforwardMeasure_cylinder_toReal_eq_integral_of_fixed) V.pushforwardMeasure φ_t (K × G) = ∫_{Gₙ(K)} J_Sφ_t(x) dV(x,S), i.e. M(φ_{t#}V ⌞ Gₙ(K)) = ∫_{Gₙ(K)} J_Sφ_t dV, a finite number because V(Gₙ(K)) < ∞ (V.finite_on_compact) and, for fixed t, (x,S) ↦ J_Sφ_t(x) is continuous, hence bounded, on the compact set K × G.

3. Regularity of the spatial derivative. Because φ is C² on the open set (−1,1) × U, the spatial derivative D(t,x) := D_xφ(t,x) (an N × N matrix) is C¹ on (−1,1) × U, and by the symmetry of second derivatives ∂_tD(t,x) = D_x(∂_tφ)(t,x). Since φ(0,·) = id on the open set U, D(0,x) = I for x ∈ U. By the velocity hypothesis ∂_tφ(0,x) = X(x) for x ∈ U, so X = ∂_tφ(0,·) is C¹ on U and ∂_tD(0,x) = DX(x) for x ∈ U.

4. The Jacobian on a short time interval (uniform o(t), no O(t²) claim). For (t,x,S) ∈ (−1,1) × U × G put g(t,x,S) := det(P_S D(t,x)ᵀD(t,x) P_S + I − P_S). With respect to the orthogonal splitting ℝ^N = S ⊕ S^⊥ this matrix is block diagonal with blocks the Gram matrix (⟨D(t,x)τ_i, D(t,x)τ_j⟩)_{i,j} (τ_1,…,τ_n an orthonormal basis of S) and the identity of S^⊥; hence g(t,x,S) = det((D(t,x)|_S)*(D(t,x)|_S)) and J_Sφ_t(x) = g(t,x,S)^{1/2}, independently of the basis. As a polynomial in the entries of D(t,x) and P_S, g is continuous on (−1,1) × U × G, C¹ in t, and ∂_tg is continuous on (−1,1) × U × G (D is C¹). Since g(0,x,S) = det I = 1 and [−1/2,1/2] × K × G is compact, uniform continuity gives t0 ∈ (0,1/2] with g ≥ 1/2 on [−t0,t0] × K × G. On this set t ↦ J_Sφ_t(x) = g^{1/2} is C¹ with ∂_tJ = ½g^{−1/2}∂_tg, which is continuous on the compact set [−t0,t0] × K × G and therefore bounded by a constant C. At t = 0, Jacobi's formula d/dt det(I + E(t))|_{t=0} = tr E'(0) for E(t) := P_S(D(t,x)ᵀD(t,x) − I)P_S (E(0) = 0 because D(0,x) = I) gives ∂_tg(0,x,S) = tr(P_S(DX(x)ᵀ + DX(x))P_S) = 2tr(P_S DX(x)) (P_S² = P_S, cyclicity of the trace), hence ∂_tJ_Sφ_t(x)|_{t=0} = tr(P_S DX(x)) = div_S X(x), which is Varifold.tangentialDivergence X x S = trace(S.1 * jacobian X x). Equivalently, J_Sφ_t(x) = 1 + t·div_S X(x) + o(t) uniformly on Gₙ(K).

5. Differentiation under the integral. For 0 < |t| ≤ t0 the mean value theorem gives |(J_Sφ_t(x) − J_Sφ_0(x))/t| ≤ C on K × G, the quotient tends to div_S X(x) as t → 0 for every (x,S) ∈ K × G (step 4), and J_Sφ_0 = 1 on K × G (D(0,·) = I). Since V(Gₙ(K)) < ∞, dominated convergence gives (1/t)(∫_{Gₙ(K)} J_Sφ_t dV − V(Gₙ(K))) → ∫_{Gₙ(K)} div_S X dV as t → 0. By step 2 the left side is the difference quotient at 0 of the real function t ↦ (V.pushforwardMeasure φ_t (K × G)).toReal (all values finite, and the value at t = 0 is V(Gₙ(K))), so this function has derivative ∫_{Gₙ(K)} div_S X dV at t = 0.

6. X vanishes with its derivative off K. On the open set U ∖ K we have φ_t = id for all t, so X = ∂_tφ(0,·) = 0 there and DX = 0 there; V vanishes off U × G (V.supported). Hence ∫_{Gₙ(K)} div_S X dV = ∫ div_S X dV = δV(X) (2.3; V.firstVariation X = ∫ tangentialDivergence X z.1 z.2 dV, the integrand being bounded on Gₙ(K) and zero V-a.e. off Gₙ(K); values of X off U are irrelevant since the derivative of X at points of the open set U only depends on X on U). This is 2.2 = 2.3: t ↦ (V.pushforwardMeasure φ_t (K ×ˢ univ)).toReal has derivative V.firstVariation X at 0.

7. 2.4. Let b be any orthonormal basis of S and extend it by an orthonormal basis (c_k) of S^⊥ to an orthonormal basis of ℝ^N. Computing the trace in this basis, Varifold.tangentialDivergence X x S = trace(P_S DX(x)) = Σ_i ⟨b_i, P_S DX(x) b_i⟩ + Σ_k ⟨c_k, P_S DX(x) c_k⟩, and the second sum vanishes because ⟨c_k, P_S w⟩ = ⟨P_S c_k, w⟩ = 0 (P_S self-adjoint, P_S c_k = 0). Moreover ⟨b_i, P_S DX(x) b_i⟩ = ⟨P_S b_i, DX(x) b_i⟩ = ⟨b_i, DX(x) b_i⟩ (P_S b_i = b_i). Hence div_S X(x) = Σ_i ⟨b_i, DX(x) b_i⟩.

8. Formal counterparts (pinned SimonGMT, kernel-checked, standard axioms only). Steps 1–6 are Varifold.hasDerivAt_pushforwardMeasure_cylinder_family_of_velocity (Poincare/SimonGMT/Chapter08/DeformationIntegral.lean:266), whose proof follows exactly this route (Varifold.hasDerivAt_integral_tangentialJacobianReal_family differentiates the Jacobian under the integral on a short time interval, and setIntegral_tangentialDivergence_initialVelocity_eq_firstVariation is step 6). Its hypotheses coincide with the contract's after (i) splitting the contract hypothesis `MapsTo … ∧ InjOn …` into its two components and (ii) passing the velocity hypothesis as `deriv (fun t ↦ φ (t, x)) 0 = X x`, which is `(h x hx).deriv` from the contract's HasDerivAt. Step 7 is Varifold.tangentialDivergence_eq_sum_inner (Chapter08/Varifold.lean:1047), whose statement is the second conjunct verbatim. This proves FirstVariationIsMassDerivative.

PART (b): FirstVariationRepresentation (2.5–2.10). Fix V with locally bounded first variation (h : V.HasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation).

9. ‖δV‖ (2.5). By the Riesz representation theorem (Ch. 1, 4.14) for the linear functional X ↦ δV(X) on K(U;ℝ^N), which satisfies |δV(X)| ≤ c_W sup|X| when spt X ⊆ W ⊂⊂ U, there is a Radon measure ‖δV‖ on U with ‖δV‖(W) = sup{|δV(X)| : |X| ≤ 1, spt X ⊆ W} for every open W ⊂⊂ U. In the contract variationMeasure V unfolds (dif_pos h) to SimonGMT's V.firstVariationRieszMeasure h, and SimonGMT's isFirstVariationMeasure_riesz (FirstVariationRiesz.lean:226) states V.IsFirstVariationMeasure (V.firstVariationRieszMeasure h): local finiteness on U, ‖δV‖(Uᶜ) = 0, and the characterization 2.5 on every open W with compact closure in U. This is the first conjunct.

10. Polar field (2.6). The same Riesz theorem gives a ‖δV‖-measurable ν with |ν| = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e. and δV(X) = −∫ ν·X d‖δV‖ for all X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N). Take ν := V.firstVariationPolarField h (FirstVariationRiesz.lean:61): it is Borel measurable (measurable_firstVariationPolarField), has ‖ν‖ = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e. (ae_firstVariationPolarField_norm_one), and isFirstVariationPolarRepresentation_riesz (FirstVariationRiesz.lean:133) gives, for every test field X, integrability of x ↦ ⟨ν x, X x⟩ w.r.t. ‖δV‖ and V.firstVariation X = −∫⟨ν, X⟩ d‖δV‖.

11. Density D_{μ_V}‖δV‖ (2.7). μ_V and ‖δV‖ are Radon measures on U; every Radon measure on an open subset of ℝ^N has the symmetric Vitali property (Besicovitch, Ch. 1 3.11(3)/3.25(1)), so by the differentiation theorem (Ch. 1, 3.23(ii)) lim_{ρ↓0} ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x))/μ_V(B_ρ(x)) exists and is finite for μ_V-a.e. x. The contract's variationDensity V x is the limsup of this ratio; where the limit exists it equals the limsup. Formally: variationDensity V unfolds to V.symmetricFirstVariationDensity (V.firstVariationRieszMeasure h) (FirstVariationDensity.lean:50) and firstVariationRiesz_symmetricDensity_spec (FirstVariationRiesz.lean:254) gives, μ_V-a.e., both the Tendsto statement and finiteness. This is the second conjunct.

12. Generalized boundary (2.8–2.9). By the Radon–Nikodym theorem in the form of Ch. 1, 3.24(iii): ‖δV‖ = (D_{μ_V}‖δV‖) μ_V + ‖δV‖ ⌞ Z with Z = {x ∈ U : D_{μ_V}‖δV‖(x) = ∞} and μ_V(Z) = 0. The contract's generalizedBoundary V, generalizedBoundaryMeasure V and generalizedMeanCurvature V ν unfold to SimonGMT's symmetricGeneralizedBoundarySet, symmetricGeneralizedBoundaryMeasure, symmetricGeneralizedMeanCurvature (FirstVariationDecomposition.lean:93,181,188) applied to the Riesz measure (and ν). firstVariationRiesz_boundary_spec gives μ_V(Z) = 0 (third conjunct).

13. Integrability and 2.10. For each test field X: firstVariationRiesz_integrable_meanCurvature_and_boundary gives integrability of ⟨H, X⟩ w.r.t. μ_V and of ⟨ν, X⟩ w.r.t. σ = ‖δV‖⌞Z (H := generalizedMeanCurvature V ν), and firstVariation_eq_meanCurvature_add_boundary_of_locallyBounded gives δV(X) = −∫⟨H,X⟩ dμ_V − ∫_{Z}⟨ν,X⟩ dσ; since σ is already the restriction of ‖δV‖ to Z, restricting σ again to Z does not change it (Measure.restrict_restrict / restrict_eq_self), so this is exactly the contract's identity δV(X) = −∫⟨H,X⟩ dμ_V − ∫⟨ν,X⟩ dσ. Mathematically this is 2.6 + 2.8: −∫ν·X d‖δV‖ = −∫H·X dμ_V − ∫_Z ν·X d‖δV‖, all integrals absolutely convergent because X is bounded with compact support in U and both measures are finite on compact subsets of U.

14. Conclusion. With ν = V.firstVariationPolarField h, steps 9–13 give every conjunct of FirstVariationRepresentation; with Part (a) this proves FirstVariationIsMassDerivative ∧ FirstVariationRepresentation.
proof_key_steps: (a) φ_t(K) ⊆ K and U ∩ φ_t⁻¹(K) = K by injectivity, so M(φ_{t#}V⌞Gₙ(K)) = ∫_{Gₙ(K)} J_Sφ_t dV (formula 2.1), finite since V(Gₙ(K)) < ∞.
C² regularity: D(t,x) = D_xφ(t,x) is C¹, D(0,·) = I and ∂_tD(0,·) = DX on U (symmetry of second derivatives, velocity hypothesis).

On a short interval [−t0,t0] the Gram determinant g = det(P_S DᵀD P_S + I − P_S) is ≥ 1/2 on [−t0,t0] × K × G, so J_Sφ_t = g^{1/2} is C¹ in t with bounded derivative and ∂_tJ|_{t=0} = tr(P_S DX) = div_S X (uniform o(t); no O(t²) remainder is claimed).

Dominated convergence on the finite measure V⌞Gₙ(K) gives d/dt|₀ ∫_{Gₙ(K)} J_Sφ_t dV = ∫_{Gₙ(K)} div_S X dV; X and DX vanish on U ∖ K, so this is δV(X) (SimonGMT hasDerivAt_pushforwardMeasure_cylinder_family_of_velocity after splitting MapsTo ∧ InjOn and converting HasDerivAt to deriv).
2.4: trace(P_S DX) = Σ⟨b_i, DX b_i⟩ for any orthonormal basis (SimonGMT tangentialDivergence_eq_sum_inner).

(b) variationMeasure V = firstVariationRieszMeasure (dif_pos); Riesz 4.14 gives IsFirstVariationMeasure (isFirstVariationMeasure_riesz) and the polar field ν (measurable, |ν| = 1 a.e., δV(X) = −∫ν·X d‖δV‖).
Differentiation theorem (Ch. 1 3.23): a.e. existence and finiteness of D_{μ_V}‖δV‖, which equals the limsup-defined variationDensity (firstVariationRiesz_symmetricDensity_spec).
Radon–Nikodym (Ch. 1 3.24(iii)): ‖δV‖ = D_{μ_V}‖δV‖ μ_V + ‖δV‖⌞Z, μ_V(Z) = 0; integrability and 2.10 from the SimonGMT symmetric decomposition lemmas, the extra restriction to Z being idempotent.

subproblem.title: Lemma 8.1.3: disintegration of a varifold along its weight (η_V^(x))
subproblem.statement: For every n-varifold V on open U ⊆ ℝ^N there is η : ℝ^N → Measure(G(N,n)) such that (i) for μ_V-a.e. x, η(x) is a probability measure and for every continuous β : G(N,n) → ℝ, (∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β(S) dV(y,S)) / μ_V(B_ρ(x)) → ∫ β dη(x) as ρ ↓ 0; and (ii) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N and continuous β ≥ 0: ∫⁻_{Gₙ(A)} β(S) dV(x,S) = ∫⁻_A (∫⁻ β dη(x)) dμ_V(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U), ∃ η : Euclidean N → Measure (Grassmannian N n), (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, IsProbabilityMeasure (η x) ∧ ∀ β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ), Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (∫ z in closedBall x ρ ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), β z.2 ∂V.measure) / (V.weight (closedBall x ρ)).toReal) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (∫ S, β S ∂(η x)))) ∧ ∀ (A : Set (Euclidean N)) (β : C(Grassmannian N n, ℝ)), MeasurableSet A → (∀ S, 0 ≤ β S) → ∫⁻ z in A ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)), ENNReal.ofReal (β z.2) ∂V.measure = ∫⁻ x in A, (∫⁻ S, ENNReal.ofReal (β S) ∂(η x)) ∂V.weight
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Lemma 1.3 and its printed proof (pp. 207–208). The printed proof is followed; details filled in: (a) the differentiation theorem “XXX Theorem 3.23 of Ch. 1” is applied to finite restrictions of μ_V to compact subsets of U (μ_V need not be locally finite at ∂U); (b) the positive functional η̃^(x) is represented by Riesz's theorem for positive functionals on the compact space G (Ch. 1 4.12) — the printed appeal to 4.14 with a “total variation measure” gives the same measure, which is moreover a probability measure; (c) the second part is stated with lintegrals of β ≥ 0 and arbitrary Borel A (both sides vanish on A ∖ U). Notation: G = Grassmannian N n (compact metric space), μ = μ_V = V.weight, B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, Gₙ(A) = A × G, 𝒦 = C(G,ℝ), 𝒦⁺ = {β ∈ 𝒦 : β ≥ 0}.

Statement. For every n-varifold V on U there is η : ℝ^N → Measure(G) such that (i) for μ-a.e. x, η(x) is a probability measure and, for every β ∈ 𝒦, ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β(S) dV(y,S) / μ(B_ρ(x)) → ∫ β dη(x) as ρ ↓ 0; (ii) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N and β ∈ 𝒦⁺: ∫⁻_{Gₙ(A)} β(S) dV(x,S) = ∫⁻_A (∫⁻ β dη(x)) dμ(x).

0. Degenerate case. If n > N then G = ∅, V.measure = 0, μ = 0; take η ≡ 0: (i) is vacuous and both sides of (ii) are 0. Assume G ≠ ∅ below; fix S0 ∈ G.

1. Countable dense family. 𝒦 with the sup norm is separable (G compact metric), so there are β_1, β_2, … ∈ 𝒦⁺ dense in 𝒦⁺; we may take β_1 ≡ 1.

Part (i) follows: for x ∉ Z and small ρ the Lean quotient (∫_{B_ρ(x) ×ˢ univ} β(z.2) dV)/ (μ(B_ρ(x))).toReal equals avg_ρ(β) (μ(B_ρ(x)) is finite and positive for small ρ, and ∫_{B_ρ(x)×G} β dV is a finite Bochner integral since β is bounded).

5. Second part (printed “follows directly from (2), (3)”). Since e(x,j) = η̃^(x)(β_j) = ∫ β_j dη(x) for x ∉ Z, (2) gives ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β_j dV = ∫_A (∫β_j dη(x)) dμ(x) for Borel A ⊆ U. subproblem.title: Compactness of Radon measures on Gₙ(U) (Simon Ch. 1 4.16, corrected), with eventual local mass bounds
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^N be open and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) measures on ℝ^N × G(N,n) such that for every compact K ⊆ U there is C_K < ∞ with μ_j(K × G(N,n)) ≤ C_K for all sufficiently large j. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and an n-varifold V on U such that ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dV for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G(N,n), ℝ) with tsupport f ⊆ U × G(N,n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (μ : ℕ → Measure (Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n)), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclidean N), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ≥0∞, C ≠ ∞ ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μ j (K ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n))) ≤ C) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∃ V : Varifold N n U, ∀ f : C_c(Euclidean N × Grassmannian N n, ℝ), tsupport f ⊆ U ×ˢ (univ : Set (Grassmannian N n)) → Tendsto (fun j ↦ ∫ z, f z ∂(μ (φ j))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ z, f z ∂V.measure))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 1, Theorem 4.16 (Compactness Theorem for Radon measures) and its printed proof (pp. 37–38), which Ch. 8 cites in 5.1 and 5.8, specialised to X = U × G (G = Grassmannian N n, compact metric). ERRATUM (GMT/Ch01 README; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_16_counterexample): 4.16 as printed (X locally compact, σ-compact, Hausdorff) is false, because the Alaoglu step yields a subnet, not a subsequence; it holds for X locally compact and second countable (= locally compact separable metrizable), which is the case here: U × G is an open subset of the separable metric space ℝ^N × G. The proof below is the printed one with the Alaoglu step made sequential via a countable dense set of test functions. A second (immaterial) adaptation: the masses are only required to be bounded eventually on each compact set (finitely many initial terms may even be infinite there), which costs nothing in a diagonal argument.

Statement. Let U ⊆ ℝ^N be open and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) measures on ℝ^N × G such that for every compact K ⊆ U there are C_K < ∞ and j_K with μ_j(K × G) ≤ C_K for all j ≥ j_K. Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and V : Varifold N n U such that ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dV.measure for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ U × G.

1. Exhaustion. If U = ∅ take φ = id and V = 0 (then every admissible f is 0). Otherwise let K_m := {y ∈ ℝ^N : |y| ≤ m, dist(y, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/m} (dist := +∞ if U = ℝ^N), so K_m is compact, K_m ⊆ interior K_{m+1}, ∪_m K_m = U. Put X_m := K_m × G (compact metric) and C_m := C_{K_m}, j_m := j_{K_m}. Every compact subset of U × G lies in some X_m (it projects to a compact subset of U, which lies in some K_m by the interior property).

2. Countable dense family. C(X_m) (continuous real functions with sup norm) is separable since X_m is a compact metric space. Hence there is a countable family 𝔉 ⊆ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport ⊆ U × G such that for every m and every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ interior(K_m) × G and every η > 0 there is g ∈ 𝔉 with tsupport g ⊆ K_{m+1} × G and sup|f − g| < η (take a countable dense subset of C(X_{m+1}) and multiply by a fixed cutoff χ_m ∈ C_c, 0 ≤ χ_m ≤ 1, χ_m = 1 on K_m × G, tsupport χ_m ⊆ interior(K_{m+1}) × G; then sup|f − χ_m h| = sup|χ_m(f − h)| ≤ sup_{X_{m+1}}|f − h|).

3. Diagonal extraction (the printed “Alaoglu + diagonal sequence” step, made sequential). For g ∈ 𝔉 with tsupport g ⊆ K_m × G and j ≥ j_m: |∫ g dμ_j| ≤ C_m sup|g|. So for each g ∈ 𝔉 the real sequence (∫ g dμ_j)_{j ≥ j_m} is bounded; enumerating 𝔉 = {g_1, g_2, …} and applying Bolzano–Weierstrass successively and then taking the diagonal sequence gives a strictly increasing φ such that L(g) := lim_j ∫ g dμ_{φ(j)} exists for every g ∈ 𝔉. (Equivalently, apply SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable / finiteMeasure_tendsto_subseq_of_compact_metrizable on each compact X_m to the finite measures μ_j⌞X_m, j ≥ j_m, and diagonalise over m.)

4. Extension to all test functions. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ U × G; then tsupport f ⊆ interior(K_m) × G for some m. Given η > 0 choose g ∈ 𝔉 with tsupport g ⊆ K_{m+1} × G and sup|f − g| < η. For j with φ(j) ≥ j_{m+1}: |∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} − ∫ g dμ_{φ(j)}| ≤ η C_{m+1}. Hence (∫ f dμ_{φ(j)})_j is Cauchy, and F(f) := lim_j ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} exists. F is linear and positive (f ≥ 0 ⇒ F(f) ≥ 0) on C_c(U × G) (identify a function on the subtype U × G with compact support with its extension by zero to ℝ^N × G, which is continuous because its support is a compact subset of the open set U × G).

5. Riesz representation (printed: “by applying Theorem 4.12”). U × G is locally compact Hausdorff (open subset of a locally compact space), so by the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani theorem (Ch. 1, 4.12; Mathlib RealRMK.rieszMeasure, integral_rieszMeasure) there is a Radon (regular, locally finite) measure λ on the subtype U × G with F(f) = ∫ f dλ for all f ∈ C_c(U × G).

6. The varifold. Define V := Varifold.ofDomainMeasure hU λ (Chapter08/Varifold.lean:409; needs IsLocallyFiniteMeasure λ), so V.measure = λ.map Subtype.val, which vanishes on Uᶜ × G and is finite on K × G for compact K ⊆ U (V is an n-varifold on U). For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G) with tsupport f ⊆ U × G: ∫ f dV.measure = ∫ f ∘ val dλ = F(f ∘ val) = lim_j ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} (the last equality because f vanishes off U × G, so ∫ f dμ_j = ∫ (f ∘ val) d(μ_j.comap val) and this is how F was defined). This is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_m of U; X_m = K_m × G compact metric.
Countable family of test functions, dense (sup norm) in C(X_{m+1})·cutoff for every m (separability of C of a compact metric space).
Bounded sequences (∫ g dμ_j)_{j ≥ j_m}; diagonal subsequence φ along which all converge (sequential form of the printed Alaoglu step; the erratum requires second countability).
Extension to all f ∈ C_c with support in U × G by uniform approximation and the eventual mass bounds; the limit F is positive linear.
Riesz–Markov–Kakutani on the locally compact space U × G gives λ; V := Varifold.ofDomainMeasure hU λ; ∫ f dV.measure = F(f).

subproblem.title: Tangent points of a varifold with nearly horizontal planes lie on countably many closed L-Lipschitz graphs (cone argument of Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐)
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, 0 < L ≤ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, V an n-varifold on U and P ∈ G(N,n), with p := Grassmannian.project P the orthogonal projection onto P and q := I − p. Then there are closed sets Γ_0, Γ_1, … ⊆ ℝ^N, each an L-Lipschitz graph over P, i.e. |q(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| (‖(y − z) − Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖ ≤ L‖Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖) for all y, z ∈ Γ_i, such that every x at which V has a tangent plane T with some multiplicity θ in the sense of Def. 8.1.1 (HasTangentPlane V x T θ) and whose plane is L/4-close to P in operator norm (|p_T v − p v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for all v) lies in some Γ_i.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (L : ℝ), 0 < L → L ≤ 1 → ∀ (U : Set (Euclidean N)) (V : Varifold N n U) (P : Grassmannian N n), ∃ Γ : ℕ → Set (Euclidean N), (∀ i, IsClosed (Γ i)) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ y ∈ Γ i, ∀ z ∈ Γ i, ‖(y - z) - Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y - z)‖) ∧ ∀ (x : Euclidean N) (T : Grassmannian N n) (θ : ℝ), HasTangentPlane V x T θ → (∀ v : Euclidean N, ‖Grassmannian.project T v - Grassmannian.project P v‖ ≤ L / 4 * ‖v‖) → ∃ i, x ∈ Γ i
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: this is the cone/Lipschitz-graph argument of Simon's printed proof of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 “⇐” (the definitions (1)–(3), estimate (9), claim (10) and the graph construction following it, printed pp. 72–74), which the printed proof of Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 invokes through “1.9 of Ch. 3” (Ch. 3, 1.9 is derived from 1.6 via Remark 1.8). Here it is run directly for the weight measure of a varifold at its tangent points in the sense of Ch. 8, Def. 1.1, with two adaptations: (a) Egoroff's theorem (printed (8)) is replaced by a countable decomposition into classes with uniform constants, so that EVERY admissible tangent point (not only almost every one) is covered; (b) the aperture of the cones is adapted to an arbitrary prescribed slope L ∈ (0,1] relative to a fixed reference plane P (the printed proof uses a fixed aperture and slope ≤ 4 relative to finitely many reference planes). Notation: μ := μ_V = V.weight; G := Grassmannian N n; for S ∈ G, p_S := Grassmannian.project S (the orthogonal projection onto S.plane: symmetric and idempotent, so |v|² = |p_S v|² + |v − p_S v|²) and q_S := I − p_S; p := p_P, q := q_P; B_r(y) := closedBall y r; H^n := μHE[n]; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞) (ω_0 = 1); V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T. “Γ is an L-graph over P” means |q(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| for all y, z ∈ Γ — in Lean notation ‖(y − z) − Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖ ≤ L * ‖Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖; “‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4” means |p_T v − p v| ≤ (L/4)|v| for every v ∈ ℝ^N.

Statement. Let N, n ∈ ℕ, 0 < L ≤ 1, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, V an n-varifold on U and P ∈ G. Then there are closed sets Γ_0, Γ_1, … ⊆ ℝ^N, each an L-graph over P, such that every x ∈ ℝ^N for which there are T ∈ G and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ and ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4 belongs to some Γ_i.

1. Consequences of Def. 1.1 at a point. Let HasTangentPlane V x T θ: x ∈ U, θ > 0, and ∫ f dV_{x,t} → θ∫ f dv(T) as t ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N × G).
 (1.1) Weight blow-ups. For g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) the function f(y,S) := g(y) lies in C_c(ℝ^N × G), because G is compact (tsupport f ⊆ tsupport g × G). By the definitions (V_{x,t} = ofReal(t^{−n}) • V.measure.map((z,S) ↦ (t^{−1}(z − x), S)), integral_map, and V.weight = V.measure.map Prod.fst), ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t^{−n}∫ g((z − x)/t) dμ(z) (for small t the integrand is supported in the compact set x + t·tsupport g ⊆ U, where μ is finite), and ∫ f dv(T) = ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n (v(T) = (H^n⌞T.plane).map(y ↦ (y,T))). Writing ν_t(A) := t^{−n}μ(x + tA), this says ∫ g dν_t → θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t ↓ 0, for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N).
 (1.2) Normalisation. T.plane has dimension n (Grassmannian.finrank_plane), so there is a linear isometry ι of ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) onto T.plane (an orthonormal basis), and H^n(ι(A)) = L^n(A) for every A ⊆ ℝ^n (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image and EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). Hence H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = L^n(B^n_κ(0)) = ω_nκ^n for κ > 0 (Measure.addHaar_closedBall; closed and open balls have the same volume).
 (1.3) Lower mass bound. For κ ∈ (0,1) take g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on B_κ(0) and tsupport g ⊆ B_1(0). Then t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)) = ν_t(B_1(0)) ≥ ∫ g dν_t → θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≥ θH^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = θω_nκ^n. Letting κ ↑ 1: liminf_{t↓0} t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)) ≥ θω_n.
 (1.4) Cone decay (n ≥ 1). For α ∈ (0,1) let K_α(T) := {v ∈ ℝ^N : |p_T v| ≤ α|v|}, a closed cone (invariant under v ↦ sv, s > 0). Then t^{−n}μ((x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_t(x)) → 0 as t ↓ 0. Indeed C := K_α(T) ∩ B_1(0) is compact, C ∩ T.plane = {0} (for v ∈ T.plane, p_T v = v, and |v| ≤ α|v| forces v = 0), and (x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_t(x) = x + tC, so the quantity equals ν_t(C). For κ ∈ (0,1] let C_κ := {v : dist(v, C) ≤ κ} (compact) and choose g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on C, tsupport g ⊆ C_κ (Urysohn). Then limsup_t ν_t(C) ≤ lim_t ∫ g dν_t = θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n ≤ θH^n(T.plane ∩ C_κ). As κ ↓ 0 the sets T.plane ∩ C_κ decrease to T.plane ∩ C = {0} (C is closed), and H^n(T.plane ∩ C_1) < ∞ by (1.2), so H^n(T.plane ∩ C_κ) → H^n({0}) = 0 (n ≥ 1). Hence ν_t(C) → 0.

2. Degenerate dimensions. If n > N there is no P ∈ G (a symmetric idempotent N × N matrix has trace ≤ N), and the claim is vacuous. If n = 0, G has exactly one element, the zero projection (a symmetric idempotent matrix of trace 0 is 0), so p = p_T = 0, q = I, and an L-graph over P is a set with at most one point. If HasTangentPlane V x T θ, then (1.3) with t^0 = 1 and ω_0 = 1 gives liminf_{t↓0} μ(B_t(x)) ≥ θ > 0; since x ∈ U, μ(B_t(x)) < ∞ for small t (V.finite_on_compact), so by continuity from above μ({x}) = lim_{t↓0} μ(B_t(x)) ≥ θ > 0: x is an atom of μ. The measure μ is σ-finite (Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite), so it has at most countably many atoms a_0, a_1, …; put Γ_i := {a_i} (and Γ_i := ∅ for unused indices). Singletons and ∅ are closed L-graphs, and every point in question is an atom, hence some a_i. This proves the claim for n = 0. Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ N from now on. (For n = N the claim is also trivial — then P is the identity, q = 0 and Γ_0 := ℝ^N works — but the argument below covers it.)

3. Linear algebra. Put c := L/4, γ := c/2 = L/8 and α := (1 − c²/16)^{1/2} = (1 − L²/256)^{1/2} ∈ (0,1). Let T ∈ G with ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4; then also |q_T v − q v| = |p v − p_T v| ≤ (L/4)|v|.
 (3.1) If v ∈ ℝ^N and |q v| > L|p v|, then v ≠ 0 and |q_T v| > c|v|. Indeed |q v|² > L²|p v|² = L²(|v|² − |q v|²) gives |q v| > L|v|/(1 + L²)^{1/2} ≥ L|v|/√2 (as L ≤ 1), so |q_T v| ≥ |q v| − (L/4)|v| > (1/√2 − 1/4)L|v| ≥ (L/4)|v|.
 (3.2) If moreover w ∈ ℝ^N with |w − v| ≤ γ|v|, then w ∈ K_α(T) and 0 < |w| ≤ 2|v|. Indeed |w| ≤ (1 + γ)|v| ≤ 2|v| and |w| ≥ (1 − γ)|v| > 0; |q_T w| ≥ |q_T v| − |q_T(w − v)| ≥ |q_T v| − |w − v| > (c − γ)|v| = (c/2)|v| ≥ (c/4)|w|; hence |p_T w|² = |w|² − |q_T w|² ≤ (1 − c²/16)|w|², i.e. |p_T w| ≤ α|w|.

4. Uniform classes (replacing Egoroff, printed (7)–(9)). For m ≥ 1 put ε_m := (2m)^{−1}(γ/2)^n/2 > 0. For m, k ≥ 1 let E_{m,k} be the set of x ∈ ℝ^N for which there are T ∈ G and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ, ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4, θ ≥ 1/m, and, for every t ∈ (0, 1/k],
 (i) μ(B_t(x)) ≥ (2m)^{−1}ω_n t^n, and (ii) μ((x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_t(x)) ≤ ε_m ω_n t^n.
 Every x with HasTangentPlane V x T θ and ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4 lies in some E_{m,k}: choose m with θ ≥ 1/m (θ > 0); by (1.3), liminf_t t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)) ≥ θω_n ≥ ω_n/m > (2m)^{−1}ω_n, and by (1.4), t^{−n}μ((x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_t(x)) → 0 < ε_mω_n; so (i) and (ii) hold for all t ∈ (0, 1/k] once k is large enough.

5. Graph property (printed (10)). CLAIM: if x, x' ∈ E_{m,k} and |x' − x| ≤ 1/(2k), then |q(x' − x)| ≤ L|p(x' − x)|. Suppose not, and put v := x' − x, s := |v|; then |q v| > L|p v|, so v ≠ 0 by (3.1) and 0 < s ≤ 1/(2k). Let T be a plane witnessing x ∈ E_{m,k}. For z ∈ B_{γs}(x') the vector w := z − x satisfies |w − v| = |z − x'| ≤ γs = γ|v|, so by (3.2) w ∈ K_α(T) and |w| ≤ 2s; that is, B_{γs}(x') ⊆ (x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_{2s}(x). Since 0 < γs ≤ 2s ≤ 1/k, (i) at x' (with t = γs) and (ii) at x (with t = 2s) give
 (2m)^{−1}ω_n(γs)^n ≤ μ(B_{γs}(x')) ≤ μ((x + K_α(T)) ∩ B_{2s}(x)) ≤ ε_mω_n(2s)^n = (2m)^{−1}ω_nγ^ns^n/2,
 which is impossible because ω_nγ^ns^n > 0. (This is the printed contradiction between (9) at the base point and the ball around the point y in (10), with the cone aperture adapted to L.)

6. Closed graph pieces (printed paragraph after (10)). Let D ⊆ ℝ^N be countable and dense (points with rational coordinates). For m, k ≥ 1 and d ∈ D put Γ_{m,k,d} := closure(E_{m,k} ∩ B_{1/(4k)}(d)). If y, z ∈ E_{m,k} ∩ B_{1/(4k)}(d), then |y − z| ≤ 1/(2k), so |q(y − z)| ≤ L|p(y − z)| by step 5; since (y,z) ↦ L|p(y − z)| − |q(y − z)| is continuous, the inequality persists on the closure. Hence each Γ_{m,k,d} is a closed L-graph over P. Every x ∈ E_{m,k} lies in B_{1/(4k)}(d) for some d ∈ D (density of D). Enumerate the countable family (Γ_{m,k,d})_{m,k ≥ 1, d ∈ D} as (Γ_i)_{i ∈ ℕ}. By step 4, every x with HasTangentPlane V x T θ and ‖p_T − p‖ ≤ L/4 lies in some E_{m,k}, hence in some Γ_i. Together with step 2 this proves the statement: ∃ Γ : ℕ → Set ℝ^N with every Γ i closed, every Γ i an L-graph over P (‖(y − z) − Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖ ≤ L‖Grassmannian.project P (y − z)‖ for y, z ∈ Γ i), and every such tangent point in some Γ i.

subproblem.title: First Rectifiability Theorem 8.1.2
subproblem.statement: Let V be an n-varifold on open U ⊆ ℝ^N such that for μ_V-a.e. x there are T ∈ G(N,n) and θ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Def. 1.1: x ∈ U, θ > 0, V_{x,λ} → θ v(T) as λ ↓ 0 against C_c(ℝ^N × G)). Let M := {x ∈ spt μ_V : ∃ T θ', HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}. Then there is θ : ℝ^N → ℝ such that for every x ∈ M some T satisfies HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x), and IsVarifoldOf V M θ: M ⊆ U is H^n-null-measurable and countably n-rectifiable, θ > 0 on M, θ is H^n-integrable on M ∩ K for every compact K ⊆ U, and V(A) = ∫_{{x ∈ M : ∃ S, M has approximate tangent plane S at x w.r.t. θ (Ch. 3 1.7), (x,S) ∈ A}} θ dH^n for all Borel A. (Exactly FirstRectifiabilityTheorem.)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 1.2 and its printed proof (p. 208), which uses Lemma 1.3 (sibling plane_disintegration) and “1.9 of Ch. 3”. ERRATUM: the printed line “η_V^(x)(β) = θ(x)β(T_x)” must read “η_V^(x)(β) = β(T_x)” (the averages in 1.3 are normalised by μ_V(B_ρ(x)), so the multiplicity cancels; the printed (1) is consistent only with the corrected value). GAP FILLED: Ch. 3, 1.9 presupposes an H^n-measurable set M and a positive locally H^n-integrable θ, whereas here only the measure μ_V is given, and the proof of 1.9 rests on both directions of Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6, neither of which is available in the pinned library. “By 1.9 of Ch. 3” is therefore expanded into Steps 2–6 below: Step 2 is the Lipschitz-graph (cone) argument of the printed proof of Ch. 3, 1.6 “⇐”, supplied by the sibling tangent_graph_cover (with L = 1); Steps 3–4 are the comparison and measurability arguments (Ch. 1, 3.3); Step 5 proves the density-one property of H^n on the carrier — the part of Ch. 3, 1.6 “⇒”/Remark 1.5(3) that is used here — directly from Lipschitz graphs of arbitrarily small slope (sibling tangent_graph_cover with L → 0), using only Lipschitz image bounds for H^n and the Lebesgue density theorem (no area formula, no Jacobians); Step 6 identifies μ_V = θ H^n ⌞ M by the Besicovitch differentiation / Radon–Nikodym theorem (Ch. 1, 3.23–3.24). “spt V” is read as spt μ_V (contract docstring). Notation: μ := μ_V = V.weight (σ-finite by Varifold.weight.instSigmaFinite; finite on compact subsets of U by V.finite_on_compact; μ(Uᶜ) = 0 by V.supported); G := Grassmannian N n (a compact metric space); p_S := Grassmannian.project S and ‖p_S − p_{S'}‖ the operator norm; H^n := μHE[n] (for natural n this is Simon's normalised H^n: SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure, Chapter02/AreaLiteral.lean:42); B_r(x) := closedBall x r; V_{x,t} := rescaledMeasure V x t; v(T) := planeVarifoldMeasure T; ω_n := unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞) (ω_0 = 1); L^n := Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n). Compact exhaustion: K_p := {x : |x| ≤ p, dist(x, ℝ^N ∖ U) ≥ 1/p} (K_p := B_p(0) if U = ℝ^N, as Lean's infDist to ∅ is 0), so each K_p is compact, K_p ⊆ interior K_{p+1}, and ∪_p K_p = U.

Statement. Suppose for μ-a.e. x there are T ∈ G and θ ∈ ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T θ (Def. 1.1: x ∈ U, θ > 0, V_{x,t} → θ v(T) against C_c(ℝ^N × G) as t ↓ 0). Let M := {x ∈ spt μ : ∃ T θ', HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}. Then there is θ : ℝ^N → ℝ with HasTangentPlane V x T (θ x) for some T at every x ∈ M, and IsVarifoldOf V M θ.

STEP 0 (consequences of Def. 1.1 at a point; uniqueness). Let HasTangentPlane V x T θ.
 (0a) x ∈ U and θ > 0 (definition).
 (0b) Weight blow-ups: for every g ∈ C_c(ℝ^N), t^{−n}∫ g((z − x)/t) dμ(z) → θ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n as t ↓ 0. (Test Def. 1.1 with f(y,S) := g(y), which is in C_c(ℝ^N × G) because G is compact; ∫ f dV_{x,t} = t^{−n}∫ g((z − x)/t) dμ(z) by Measure.map / integral_map and μ = V.measure.map Prod.fst, and ∫ f dv(T) = ∫_{T.plane} g dH^n.)
 (0c) Density: HasDensity n μ x θ, i.e. μ(B_t(x))/(ω_nt^n) → θ. Indeed H^n⌞T.plane is the image of L^n under a linear isometry of ℝ^n onto T.plane (Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so H^n(T.plane ∩ B_κ(0)) = ω_nκ^n for κ > 0. Testing (0b) with g ∈ C_c, 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g = 1 on B_κ(0), tsupport g ⊆ B_1(0) (κ < 1) gives liminf_t t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)) ≥ θω_nκ^n; testing with g = 1 on B_1(0), tsupport g ⊆ B_κ(0) (κ > 1) gives limsup_t t^{−n}μ(B_t(x)) ≤ θω_nκ^n; let κ → 1. In particular μ(B_t(x)) > 0 for every t > 0, so x ∈ spt μ; hence M = {x : ∃ T θ', HasTangentPlane V x T θ'}.
 (0d) Uniqueness: if also HasTangentPlane V x T' θ', then θ = θ' (both equal the density by (0c)), and θH^n⌞T.plane = θ'H^n⌞T'.plane as measures (both are the vague limit of the same weight blow-ups by (0b); they are locally finite Borel measures on ℝ^N, so Measure.ext_of_integral_eq_on_compactlySupported applies). Hence H^n⌞T.plane = H^n⌞T'.plane; their supports are T.plane and T'.plane (SimonGMT Chapter03.support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule), so T.plane = T'.plane and T = T' (Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq). For x ∈ M let θ(x) > 0 and T(x) ∈ G be these unique values, and put θ(x) := 0 for x ∉ M. Then HasTangentPlane V x T(x) (θ x) for every x ∈ M (the first conclusion), θ > 0 on M, and M ⊆ U.
 (0e) μ(ℝ^N ∖ M) = 0 (outer measure): ℝ^N ∖ M = {x : ¬∃ T θ, HasTangentPlane V x T θ}, which is μ-null by hypothesis.
 (0f) Borel representative of θ: for r > 0, x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is Borel (Tonelli for the s-finite μ; SimonGMT Chapter01.measurable_closedBall_mass_of_sFinite), so Θ̂(x) := liminf_{k→∞} densityRatio n μ x (1/(k+1)) is a Borel function ℝ^N → [0,∞], and by (0c), θ(x) = (Θ̂(x)).toReal for every x ∈ M.

STEP 1 (degenerate dimensions). If n > N then G = ∅, so V.measure = 0 (a measure on the empty space ℝ^N × ∅), μ = 0 and M = ∅; IsVarifoldOf V ∅ θ holds trivially (∅ ⊆ U, ∅ is null-measurable, countably rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, positivity and integrability are vacuous, and both sides of the identity are 0). If n = 0: by (0c) (ω_0 = 1, t^0 = 1), μ({x}) = lim_{t↓0} μ(B_t(x)) = θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (μ(B_t(x)) < ∞ for small t as x ∈ U), so M consists of atoms of the σ-finite measure μ and is countable; hence M is Borel, CountablyRectifiable 0 M (each point is the range of a constant map ℝ^0 → ℝ^N, with M₀ = ∅), and by (0e) μ = Σ_{x∈M} θ(x)δ_x = θ H^0⌞M (μHE[0] = μH[0] is the counting measure, Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero); in particular for compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^0 = μ(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞, and every μ-null subset of M is empty. Steps 7–9 below then apply verbatim, with “Step 6” replaced by this paragraph. Assume n ≥ 1 in Steps 2–6.

STEP 2 (countable rectifiability; printed “M is … countably n-rectifiable”). G is compact and S ↦ p_S is continuous into the operators, so there are P_1, …, P_J ∈ G such that every T ∈ G satisfies ‖p_T − p_{P_j}‖ ≤ 1/4 for some j. The sibling tangent_graph_cover with L = 1 and P = P_j gives closed sets Γ_{j,i} (i ∈ ℕ), each a 1-graph over P_j (|q_j(y − z)| ≤ |p_j(y − z)| for y, z ∈ Γ_{j,i}, where p_j := p_{P_j}, q_j := I − p_j), such that every x ∈ M (with T := T(x), which is within 1/4 of some P_j) lies in some Γ_{j,i}. On Γ := Γ_{j,i}: |y − z|² = |p_j(y − z)|² + |q_j(y − z)|² ≤ 2|p_j(y − z)|², so p_j is injective on Γ and its inverse h : p_j(Γ) → Γ is √2-Lipschitz. Let ι_j be a linear isometry of ℝ^n onto P_j.plane (orthonormal basis; finrank = n). The map a ↦ h(ι_j a) on ι_j^{−1}(p_j(Γ)) is √2-Lipschitz; extending each of its N real coordinates by McShane's formula (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real, Topology/MetricSpace/Lipschitz.lean:308; or SimonGMT exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional, Chapter02/AreaDomain.lean) gives a Lipschitz F_{j,i} : ℝ^n → ℝ^N with Γ ⊆ range F_{j,i}. Re-indexing the countable family by ℕ, M ⊆ ∪ range F_{j,i}: CountablyRectifiable n M (with M₀ = ∅).

STEP 3 (comparison of μ and H^n on M).
 (3a) If Z ⊆ M and H^n(Z) = 0, then μ(Z) = 0. Fix k ∈ ℕ and τ > 0, and put Z_k := {x ∈ Z : θ(x) ≤ k}, Z_{k,δ} := {x ∈ Z_k : μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k + τ)ω_nρ^n for 0 < ρ ≤ δ}; by (0c), Z_k = ∪_{j≥1} Z_{k,1/j}. Since H^n(Z_{k,δ}) = 0, for every ζ > 0 there is a countable cover of Z_{k,δ} by sets C_i of diameters d_i < δ with Σ_i ω_n(d_i/2)^n < ζ (definition of Simon's normalised H^n). Discard the C_i not meeting Z_{k,δ} and pick x_i ∈ C_i ∩ Z_{k,δ}; then C_i ⊆ B_{d_i}(x_i) and μ(B_{d_i}(x_i)) ≤ (k + τ)ω_nd_i^n (if d_i = 0, then μ({x_i}) ≤ (k + τ)ω_nρ^n for all small ρ > 0, so μ({x_i}) = 0). Hence μ(Z_{k,δ}) ≤ Σ_i (k + τ)ω_nd_i^n = 2^n(k + τ)Σ_i ω_n(d_i/2)^n < 2^n(k + τ)ζ for every ζ > 0, so μ(Z_{k,δ}) = 0, and μ(Z) ≤ Σ_{k,j} μ(Z_{k,1/j}) = 0.
 (3b) Let m ≥ 1 and let Z ⊆ ℝ^N be contained in some K_p, with μ(Z) = 0 and limsup_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(y))/(ω_nρ^n) ≥ 1/m for every y ∈ Z. Then H^n(Z) = 0. Indeed μ⌞interior(K_{p+1}) is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N, hence outer regular, so for every ζ > 0 there is an open O with Z ⊆ O ⊆ interior(K_{p+1}) and μ(O) < ζ. For y ∈ Z the upper density of μ⌞O at y equals that of μ (small balls about y lie in O), so Simon's comparison theorem Ch. 1, 3.3 (SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_3 with A₁ := Z, A₂ := O, t := 1/m; its density is the upper density of μ restricted to A₂) gives (1/m)H^n(Z) ≤ μ(O) < ζ. (SimonGMT states 3.3 for Simon's Gamma-normalised Hausdorff outer measure simonHausdorffOuterMeasureReal n and density quotients normalised by realUnitBallVolume n; for natural n these are μHE[n] and ω_n by Chapter01.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_toOuterMeasure, Chapter02.simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure and Chapter01.volume_euclidean_ball_eq (n ≥ 1). Its Borel-regularity hypothesis holds for the outer measure of the Borel measure μ⌞interior(K_{p+1}) (every set has a measurable superset of the same measure, toMeasurable); alternatively the underlying Chapter01.mul_simonHausdorff_le_of_le_dimensionalUpperDensity only needs Borel sets to be Carathéodory-measurable.) Hence H^n(Z) = 0. Consequence: every μ-null set Z ⊆ M is H^n-null (apply (3b) to the pieces Z ∩ K_p ∩ {θ ≥ 1/m}, using (0c), and take the countable union over p, m).

STEP 4 (H^n-measurability of M; printed “M is H^n-measurable”). For m, k ≥ 1 let F_{m,k} := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≥ 1/m and μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (2m)^{−1}ω_nρ^n for 0 < ρ ≤ 1/k}; by (0c), M = ∪_{m,k} F_{m,k}. Choose countably many closed balls B_r(x_0) (x_0 ∈ ℚ^N, r ∈ ℚ_{>0}, B_{2r}(x_0) ⊆ U) covering U, and for each put E := F_{m,k} ∩ B_r(x_0), whose closure cl E ⊆ B_r(x_0) is a compact subset of U (contained in some K_p). For y ∈ cl E write y = lim x_i with x_i ∈ E; for 0 < ρ ≤ 1/k and i large, B_{ρ − |x_i − y|}(x_i) ⊆ B_ρ(y), so μ(B_ρ(y)) ≥ (2m)^{−1}ω_n(ρ − |x_i − y|)^n → (2m)^{−1}ω_nρ^n; thus the upper density of μ is ≥ (2m)^{−1} at every point of cl E. Since μ(cl E ∖ M) = 0 by (0e), (3b) (with 2m in place of m) gives H^n(cl E ∖ M) = 0. Hence M ∩ cl E = cl E ∖ (cl E ∖ M) is a closed set minus an H^n-null set, so it is H^n-null-measurable, and M = ∪(M ∩ cl E) (countable union over m, k and the balls; E ⊆ M ∩ cl E ⊆ M) is null-measurable: NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n].

STEP 5 (density one of H^n on the carrier). For p ≥ 1 let M_p := {x ∈ M : θ(x) ≥ 1/p} ∩ K_p; it is H^n-null-measurable (Step 4, and θ = Θ̂.toReal on M with Θ̂ Borel, (0f)). The upper density of μ is ≥ 1/p on M_p, so Ch. 1, 3.3 (with A₁ := M_p, A₂ := interior K_{p+1}) gives H^n(M_p) ≤ p·μ(interior K_{p+1}) < ∞. Let λ_p := H^n⌞M_p, a finite Borel measure on ℝ^N. CLAIM: lim_{r↓0} λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) = 1 for λ_p-a.e. x.
 Fix L ∈ (0,1]. As in Step 2 choose P_1, …, P_J ∈ G such that every T ∈ G satisfies ‖p_T − p_{P_j}‖ ≤ L/4 for some j, and apply the sibling tangent_graph_cover with this L to each P_j: closed L-graphs Γ_{j,i} over P_j (i ∈ ℕ) such that every x ∈ M lies in some Γ_{j,i}. Fix one Γ := Γ_{j,i}, write P := P_j, p := p_P, q := I − p, and A := M_p ∩ Γ (H^n-null-measurable).
 (i) Graph comparison. For z, x ∈ Γ, |p(z) − p(x)| ≤ |z − x| ≤ (1 + L²)^{1/2}|p(z) − p(x)|, because |z − x|² = |p(z − x)|² + |q(z − x)|² ≤ (1 + L²)|p(z − x)|². So p is injective on Γ and h := (p|_Γ)^{−1} : p(Γ) → Γ is (1 + L²)^{1/2}-Lipschitz. For x ∈ A, r > 0 and s := r(1 + L²)^{−1/2} we have p(A) ∩ B_s(p x) ⊆ p(A ∩ B_r(x)) ⊆ p(A) ∩ B_r(p x) and A ∩ B_r(x) = h(p(A ∩ B_r(x))). Since H^n does not increase under the 1-Lipschitz map p and increases at most by the factor (1 + L²)^{n/2} under h (Mathlib LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le / LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le, MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:733,745; μHE[n] is a constant multiple of μH[n]; these bounds hold for arbitrary sets),

 (ii) Lebesgue density in the plane. Let ι be a linear isometry of ℝ^n onto P.plane. Then H^n(ι(B)) = L^n(B) for every B ⊆ ℝ^n and ι^{−1}(B_s(ι b)) = B^n_s(b), so H^n(P.plane ∩ B_s(a)) = ω_ns^n for a ∈ P.plane. By the Lebesgue density theorem in ℝ^n for the set ι^{−1}(p(A)) (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div with μ = volume, Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1105, valid for arbitrary sets), there is an H^n-null set N_A ⊆ p(A) such that H^n(p(A) ∩ B_s(a))/(ω_ns^n) → 1 as s ↓ 0 for every a ∈ p(A) ∖ N_A. The set of x ∈ A with p(x) ∈ N_A is h(N_A), of H^n-measure ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2}H^n(N_A) = 0.
 (iii) Lebesgue density of Γ for λ_p. By Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div for the finite measure λ_p and the closed set Γ, for λ_p-a.e. x ∈ Γ: λ_p(B_r(x)) > 0 for r > 0 and λ_p(Γ ∩ B_r(x))/λ_p(B_r(x)) → 1 as r ↓ 0; moreover λ_p(Γ ∩ B_r(x)) = H^n(A ∩ B_r(x)).
 (iv) Combining (i)–(iii): for λ_p-a.e. x ∈ A, (1 + L²)^{−n/2} ≤ liminf_r H^n(A ∩ B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) ≤ limsup_r H^n(A ∩ B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2} and λ_p(B_r(x)) = (1 + o(1))H^n(A ∩ B_r(x)); hence (1 + L²)^{−n/2} ≤ liminf_r λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) ≤ limsup_r λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) ≤ (1 + L²)^{n/2}. Since M_p ⊆ M ⊆ ∪_{j,i}Γ_{j,i} (countably many graphs), these two-sided bounds hold for λ_p-a.e. x ∈ M_p, i.e. λ_p-a.e. Taking L = 1/l for l = 1, 2, … and intersecting the countably many full-measure sets proves the CLAIM.

STEP 6 (μ = θ H^n ⌞ M; printed “μ_V = H^n ⌞ θ in U”). Fix p and let ρ_p := μ⌞M_p, a finite measure (ρ_p(ℝ^N) ≤ μ(K_p) < ∞).
 (a) ρ_p ≪ λ_p: if λ_p(Z) = 0 then H^n(Z ∩ M_p) = 0, so μ(Z ∩ M_p) = 0 by (3a).
 (b) By the Besicovitch differentiation theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_rnDeriv, Covering/Besicovitch.lean:1078) for the finite measures ρ_p and λ_p, for λ_p-a.e. x, ρ_p(B_r(x))/λ_p(B_r(x)) → (dρ_p/dλ_p)(x) as r ↓ 0; by (a) and the Radon–Nikodym theorem, ρ_p = (dρ_p/dλ_p)·λ_p (Measure.withDensity_rnDeriv_eq).
 (c) For λ_p-a.e. x ∈ M_p: (α) λ_p(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) → 1 (Step 5); (β) μ(M_p ∩ B_r(x))/μ(B_r(x)) → 1 — this holds for μ-a.e. x ∈ M_p by Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div applied to the finite measure μ⌞interior(K_{p+1}) (which agrees with μ on small balls about points of M_p ⊆ K_p) and the set M_p, and its exceptional set is a μ-null subset of M, hence H^n-null by (3b), hence λ_p-null; (γ) μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nr^n) → θ(x) (0c).  (d) Since θ > 0 on M and M ⊆ U = ∪_p K_p, the sets M_p increase to M; by monotone convergence μ⌞M = θ·H^n⌞M, and with (0e), μ(B) = ∫_{B ∩ M} θ dH^n for every Borel B ⊆ ℝ^N (and then for every μ-null-measurable B). θ is (H^n⌞M)-a.e. measurable (θ = Θ̂.toReal on M, (0f)), and for compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n = μ(M ∩ K) ≤ μ(K) < ∞: IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n].

STEP 7 (approximate tangent planes w.r.t. θ, Ch. 3, 1.7, at every x ∈ M). Let x ∈ M and f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N) with tsupport f ⊆ B_R(0). For r > 0 with B_{rR}(x) ⊆ U, the homothety z ↦ (z − x)/r = blowUpMap x r z scales H^n by the factor r^{−n} (Mathlib euclideanHausdorffMeasure_homothety_image / _preimage), so ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' M} f(y)θ(x + ry) dH^n(y) = r^{−n}∫_M f((z − x)/r)θ(z) dH^n(z) = r^{−n}∫ f((z − x)/r) dμ(z) (Step 6(d); the integrands are bounded Borel functions times θ, supported in the compact set B_{rR}(x) ⊆ U where θ is H^n⌞M-integrable and μ is finite, so these Bochner integrals are integrals of integrable functions), and this tends to θ(x)∫_{T(x).plane} f dH^n by (0b). Since finrank T(x).plane = n, this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T(x).plane. By HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (Chapter03/Rectifiable.lean; θ(x) ≠ 0) and Grassmannian.eq_of_plane_eq, for every x ∈ M and S ∈ G: HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane ⇔ S = T(x).

STEP 8 (V is the graph varifold; printed (1)–(2), with the erratum). Let η be given by the sibling plane_disintegration (Lemma 1.3). For μ-a.e. x we have x ∈ M, η(x) a probability measure and avg_ρ(β) := ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x))} β dV / μ(B_ρ(x)) → ∫β dη(x) for all β ∈ C(G). At such x, avg_ρ(β) = ∫_{B_1(0)×G} β(S) dV_{x,ρ} / V_{x,ρ}(B_1(0) × G) (change of variables), and V_{x,ρ} → θ(x) v(T(x)) with θ(x) v(T(x))(∂B_1(0) × G) = θ(x)H^n(T(x).plane ∩ ∂B_1(0)) = 0 (n ≥ 1: the unit sphere of the n-plane is H^n-null; n = 0: T(x).plane ∩ ∂B_1(0) = ∅).  (1) ∫_{Gₙ(A)} β(S) dV(x,S) = ∫_{M∩A} β(T(x)) dμ(x).
 x ↦ T(x) is μ-a.e. equal to a Borel map: with β_{ab}(S) := S_{ab} (matrix entries, continuous), T(x)_{ab} = ∫β_{ab} dη(x) = lim_k ∫_{Gₙ(B_{1/k}(x))} S_{ab} dV / μ(B_{1/k}(x)), a limit of Borel functions of x (Tonelli for the σ-finite V and the bounded integrand 1_{|y−x|≤1/k}S_{ab}); set T̃(x) := this limit where it exists and lies in G (a Borel set of x), and a fixed S0 ∈ G otherwise. Then T̃ is Borel and T̃ = T μ-a.e. The measures V and ν := μ.map(x ↦ (x, T̃(x))) on ℝ^N × G both vanish on Uᶜ × G and are finite on K × G for compact K ⊆ U; by (1) they agree on all integrals of 1_A(x)β(S) (A Borel, β ∈ C(G), β ≥ 0), hence on all rectangles A × B (A ⊆ K_m Borel, B ⊆ G closed, using continuous β_k ↓ 1_B and dominated convergence; then all Borel B by the π-λ theorem). Hence V = ν (Measure.ext_of_generateFrom_of_iUnion) — this is the printed (2).

STEP 9 (assembly). For Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G: V(A) = ν(A) = μ({x : (x, T̃(x)) ∈ A}) = μ({x ∈ M : (x, T(x)) ∈ A}) (μ is carried by M by (0e), and T̃ = T μ-a.e.) = ∫⁻_{{x ∈ M : (x,T(x)) ∈ A}} θ dH^n (Step 6(d); this set differs from the null-measurable set M ∩ {x : (x, T̃(x)) ∈ A} by a μ-null subset of M, which is H^n-null by (3b)) = ∫⁻_{{x ∈ M : ∃ S, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x S.plane ∧ (x,S) ∈ A}} ofReal(θ x) dμHE[n] (Step 7: the two sets coincide). Together with M ⊆ U (0d), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] (Step 4), CountablyRectifiable n M (Step 2), θ > 0 on M (0d), and IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ K) μHE[n] for compact K ⊆ U (Step 6(d)), this is IsVarifoldOf V M θ; with the first conclusion from (0d) this proves FirstRectifiabilityTheorem.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, 3.1–3.4 (printed pp. 210–211), “by essentially the same computation as in §4 of Ch. 4”, i.e. Ch. 4, 3.1–3.10 and 4.7, with the radial test field X_y = γ(r)(y − x), γ(r) = φ(r/ρ). Errata/normalisations: (i) the printed 3.3 is a subtraction; the contract states it additively in [0,∞], which is equivalent because every term is finite (B_ρ(x) is compact in U); (ii) 3.4 needs no locally-bounded-first-variation hypothesis, only stationarity in B_{ρ0}(x); (iii) the sign of δV(X) in the radial identity is “−δV(X)” (SimonGMT WeightedRadialIdentity.lean, header), which is irrelevant below because only |δV(X)| is used or δV(X) = 0. Notation: μ = μ_V = V.weight, ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V, B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ (closed), B°_ρ(x) = ball x ρ (open), r = |y − x|, ω_n = unitBallVolume n ∈ (0,∞) (ω_0 = 1), densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n) (note ofReal ρ ^ n = ofReal (ρ^n) for ρ ≥ 0), and for (y,S) ∈ ℝ^N × G: p_{S⊥}(v) = v − p_S(v); the contract's normalDefect V x A = ∫_{Gₙ(A)} |p_{S⊥}(y − x)|²/|y − x|^{n+2} dV with the Lean convention 0/0 = 0 at y = x.

COMMON COMPUTATION (3.2). Let x ∈ U, R > 0 with B_R(x) ⊆ U, ε ∈ (0,1) and φ ∈ C¹(ℝ) with φ' ≤ 0, φ = 1 on (−∞,1], φ = 0 on [1+ε, ∞). For 0 < ρ with (1+ε)ρ < R put X_ρ(y) = φ(|y−x|/ρ)(y − x); X_ρ is C¹ (φ is constant near 0), with support in B_{(1+ε)ρ}(x) ⊆ B°_R(x), so X_ρ ∈ K(U;ℝ^N). Put I(ρ) = ∫φ(r/ρ) dμ and J(ρ) = ∫ φ(r/ρ) |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² dV(y,S) (integrand 0 at y = x).
C1. For S ∈ G and y ≠ x: div_S X_ρ = nφ(r/ρ) + r ∂_r[φ(r/ρ)] (1 − |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|²), because trace p_S = n and ∇^S r = p_S((y−x)/r) (this is 3.2: Σ e_S^{ij}(x^i−y^i)(x^j−y^j)/r² = 1 − |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|²); at y = x, div_S X_ρ = n = nφ(0).
C2. r ∂_r[φ(r/ρ)] = (r/ρ)φ'(r/ρ) = −ρ ∂_ρ[φ(r/ρ)]. I and J are C¹ in ρ (differentiation under the integral, dominated by sup|φ'|·(1+ε)/ρ times the finite mass of B_R(x)), and integrating C1 against V gives δV(X_ρ) = nI(ρ) − ρI'(ρ) + ρJ'(ρ), i.e.
   d/dρ (ρ^{-n} I(ρ)) = ρ^{-n} J'(ρ) − ρ^{-n-1} δV(X_ρ).        (★)
   (Formal: SimonGMT Varifold.hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass, WeightedRadialIdentity.lean:200, with h ≡ 1, which uses the squared-radius profile t ↦ φ(t/ρ²) — any such C¹ profile works identically; the gradient term vanishes for h ≡ 1.)
C3. J'(ρ) ≥ 0 since ∂_t[φ(r/t)] = −(r/t²)φ'(r/t) ≥ 0. Moreover ∂_t[φ(r/t)] vanishes unless 1 ≤ r/t ≤ 1+ε, i.e. r/(1+ε) ≤ t ≤ r, where r^{-n} ≤ t^{-n} ≤ (1+ε)^n r^{-n}; hence (Fubini, g := |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² ∈ [0,1]) for 0 < σ ≤ ρ: ∫ r^{-n}(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ)) g dV ≤ ∫_σ^ρ t^{-n} J'(t) dt ≤ (1+ε)^n ∫ r^{-n}(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ)) g dV (this is Ch. 4, 3.5, with the inequalities written in the direction forced by t ≤ r on the support). Take a family φ = φ_ε decreasing as ε ↓ 0 to the indicator of (−∞,1]. Then φ(r/ρ) → 1_{r≤ρ}, φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ) → 1_{σ<r≤ρ} pointwise, I(ρ) → μ(B_ρ(x)), and (dominated convergence: for ε ≤ ε0 with (1+ε0)ρ < R the integrands are bounded by σ^{-n}·1_{B_{(1+ε0)ρ}(x)}, which has finite V-mass because B_{(1+ε0)ρ}(x) ⊆ B_R(x) ⊆ U) both bounds converge to ∫_{Gₙ(B_ρ(x)∖B_σ(x))} r^{-n}|p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² dV = normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x) ∖ B_σ(x)) (note r^{-n}|p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² = |p_{S⊥}(y−x)|²/r^{n+2}).

PART A: MonotonicityFormula (3.3). Hypotheses: V has locally bounded first variation, 0 < ρ0, B°_{ρ0}(x) ⊆ U, Λ ≥ 0, and (3.1) ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Λ μ(B_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ0.
A1. Open balls. For 0 < s ≤ ρ0: B°_s(x) = ∪_{s'<s} B_{s'}(x), so by continuity from below ‖δV‖(B°_s(x)) ≤ Λ μ(B°_s(x)).
A2. Bound on δV(X_ρ) (uses 2.6 from the sibling first_variation: δV(X) = −∫ν·X d‖δV‖ with |ν| = 1 ‖δV‖-a.e., ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V). Hence |δV(X_ρ)| ≤ ∫|X_ρ| d‖δV‖ ≤ (1+ε)ρ ∫φ(r/ρ) d‖δV‖. By the layer-cake formula and since {y : φ(|y−x|/ρ) > s} = B°_{ρ a_s}(x) with a_s ∈ (1, 1+ε] for s ∈ (0,1) (φ is continuous, non-increasing, = 1 on [0,1]), A1 gives, when (1+ε)ρ ≤ ρ0: ∫φ(r/ρ) d‖δV‖ = ∫_0^1 ‖δV‖(B°_{ρa_s}(x)) ds ≤ Λ ∫_0^1 μ(B°_{ρa_s}(x)) ds = Λ I(ρ). So |δV(X_ρ)| ≤ Λ_ε ρ I(ρ), Λ_ε := (1+ε)Λ.
A3. Integrating factor. From (★) and A2: d/dρ(ρ^{-n}I) ≥ ρ^{-n}J' − Λ_ε ρ^{-n} I, hence d/dρ(e^{Λ_ε ρ} ρ^{-n} I(ρ)) = e^{Λ_ερ}(d/dρ(ρ^{-n}I) + Λ_ε ρ^{-n}I) ≥ e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{-n}J'(ρ) ≥ ρ^{-n}J'(ρ) ≥ 0, for 0 < ρ < ρ0/(1+ε).
A4. Integrate over [σ, ρ] (0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0/(1+ε)): e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{-n}I(ρ) − e^{Λ_εσ}σ^{-n}I(σ) ≥ ∫_σ^ρ e^{Λ_εt}t^{-n}J'(t) dt ≥ ∫_σ^ρ t^{-n}J'(t) dt ≥ ∫ r^{-n}(φ(r/ρ) − φ(r/σ))|p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|² dV (A3, e^{Λ_εt} ≥ 1, J' ≥ 0, C3). Given 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0, every small ε satisfies (1+ε)ρ < ρ0; letting ε ↓ 0 (C3) yields, with all terms finite (B_ρ(x) ⊆ B°_{ρ0}(x) ⊆ U compact):
   e^{Λσ}σ^{-n}μ(B_σ(x)) + normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x) ∖ B_σ(x)) ≤ e^{Λρ}ρ^{-n}μ(B_ρ(x)).        (3.3)
A5. Conclusions. Dividing (3.3) by ω_n gives the second inequality of the contract. Since the defect is ≥ 0, ρ ↦ e^{Λρ}μ(B_ρ(x))/ρ^n is monotone on (0,ρ0) (the contract's MonotoneOn, in ℝ≥0∞). A monotone function has a limit at 0+, so θ := lim_{σ↓0} e^{Λσ}densityRatio n μ x σ exists, and since e^{Λσ} → 1, HasDensity n μ x θ holds (Tendsto densityRatio (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝 θ)); θ ≤ e^{Λσ}densityRatio(σ) for every σ ∈ (0,ρ0) (monotone limit from above), and θ ≠ ∞ because densityRatio(σ) < ∞ (μ(B_σ(x)) < ∞, ω_n σ^n > 0). This is MonotonicityFormula. (For n = 0 all statements hold as well: ω_0 = 1, ρ^0 = 1, and the defect integrand equals 1 off y = x.)

PART B: StationaryMonotonicityIdentity (3.4). Hypotheses: 0 < ρ0, B°_{ρ0}(x) ⊆ U, δV(X) = 0 for every X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N) with tsupport X ⊆ B°_{ρ0}(x). No first-variation bound is used.
B1. For (1+ε)ρ < ρ0, X_ρ is such a field, so δV(X_ρ) = 0 and (★) reads d/dρ(ρ^{-n}I) = ρ^{-n}J'. Integrating and letting ε ↓ 0 with the two-sided bounds C3 gives, for 0 < σ ≤ ρ < ρ0, the identity
   σ^{-n}μ(B_σ(x)) + normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x) ∖ B_σ(x)) = ρ^{-n}μ(B_ρ(x)).
   (Formal: SimonGMT StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity, StationaryMonotonicity.lean:131, applied with any R ∈ (ρ, ρ0): closedBall x R ⊆ ball x ρ0 ⊆ U and V is StationaryOn (ball x R); its normalizedBallMass is μ(B_ρ)/ofReal(ρ^n) and its annularMonotonicityDefect equals normalDefect on the annulus because |p_{S⊥}(y−x)|²/r^{n+2} = radialNormalSq/r^n off y = x, via Grassmannian.normalProject_eq_sub and norm_normalProject_radial_sq, RadialFirstVariation.lean:81,123.)
B2. In particular σ ↦ σ^{-n}μ(B_σ(x)) is non-decreasing on (0,ρ0), so L := lim_{σ↓0} σ^{-n}μ(B_σ(x)) exists (StationaryOn.tendsto_normalizedBallMass_atRight) and θ := L/ω_n satisfies HasDensity n μ x θ.
B3. Fix ρ ∈ (0,ρ0). As σ ↓ 0 the sets B_ρ(x) ∖ B_σ(x) increase to B_ρ(x) ∖ {x}; by monotone convergence normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x)∖B_σ(x)) → normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x) ∖ {x}) = normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x)), the centre contributing 0 because the integrand there is ofReal(0/0) = 0. Passing to the limit in B1 and dividing by ω_n: θ + ω_n^{-1} normalDefect V x (B_ρ(x)) = densityRatio n μ x ρ, which is StationaryMonotonicityIdentity (all terms finite). (Again valid for n = 0: then the integrand is 1 off the centre and the identity reads μ({x}) + μ(B_ρ(x)∖{x}) = μ(B_ρ(x)).)

PART C: DensityExistsAE (3.6). Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Lemma 3.6 and its printed proof (p. 211). No erratum; one detail is filled in: the printed claim “μ_V(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_{y→x} μ_V(B_ρ(y))” (which needs finiteness of μ_V on a slightly larger ball) is replaced, for the Borel measurability of x ↦ μ_V(B_ρ(x)), by Tonelli's theorem, which holds for every x. Notation: μ = μ_V = V.weight, ‖δV‖ = variationMeasure V, B_ρ(x) = closedBall x ρ, densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_n ρ^n). Hypothesis: V has locally bounded first variation in U.

L1. A.e. ball bound (the parenthetical remark of 3.6, from Ch. 1 3.23). By 2.7 (sibling first_variation, second conjunct of FirstVariationRepresentation), for μ-a.e. x the ratio ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x))/μ(B_ρ(x)) converges as ρ ↓ 0 to the finite value D(x) := variationDensity V x. Also μ(Uᶜ) = 0 (V.supported) and μ(ℝ^N ∖ spt μ) = 0. Fix such an x with x ∈ U ∩ spt μ. Choose ρ1 > 0 with B_{ρ1}(x) ⊆ U (U open) and Λ' > D(x) finite; for small ρ the ratio is < Λ', i.e. ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Λ' μ(B_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ2. Hence there are ρ0 ∈ (0, min(ρ1,ρ2)) and Λ(x) ≥ 0 with ball x ρ0 ⊆ U and ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Λ(x) μ(B_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ0, which is hypothesis 3.1 at x. (Formal shortcut: SimonGMT Varifold.ae_exists_ballFirstVariationBound_inside, Chapter08/BallVariationBound.lean:66, gives μ-a.e. R > 0, Λ ≥ 0 with closedBall x R ⊆ U and the bound for 0 < r < R, stated with firstVariationRieszMeasure, which is variationMeasure V by dif_pos.)

L2. Existence and finiteness (first part of 3.6, “follows directly from the monotonicity formula 3.3”). At every x as in L1, Part A above (MonotonicityFormula, applied with ρ0 and Λ := Λ(x)) gives θ_x ∈ [0,∞) with HasDensity n μ x θ_x. Thus for μ-a.e. x, Θ^n(μ, x) exists and is finite.

L3. Borel measurability of the ball mass. μ is σ-finite (V.measure is σ-finite: Varifold.measure.instSigmaFinite, and μ is its image under Prod.fst, finite on the compact exhaustion of U and zero off U). For fixed ρ > 0 the set {(x,y) : |y − x| ≤ ρ} is closed in ℝ^N × ℝ^N, so by Tonelli (measurability of x ↦ ∫ 1_{|y−x|≤ρ} dμ(y) for s-finite μ; Mathlib Measurable.lintegral_prod_right'), x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is Borel measurable on ℝ^N with values in [0,∞]. Hence x ↦ densityRatio n μ x ρ = μ(B_ρ(x)) · (ω_n ρ^n)^{-1} is Borel for every fixed ρ > 0.

L4. Borel representative. Define Θ(x) := liminf_{k→∞} densityRatio n μ x (1/(k+1)) ∈ [0,∞]. As a liminf of a sequence of Borel functions with values in ℝ≥0∞, Θ is Borel measurable (Measurable.liminf).

L5. Agreement a.e. If HasDensity n μ x θ_x holds (Tendsto densityRatio n μ x along 𝓝[>]0 to θ_x), then along the particular sequence 1/(k+1) → 0+ the ratios converge to θ_x, so Θ(x) = θ_x. By L2 this holds for μ-a.e. x, and there θ_x ≠ ∞. Hence for μ-a.e. x: Θ x ≠ ∞ ∧ HasDensity n μ x (Θ x). This is DensityExistsAE (“Θ^n(μ_V,·) is μ_V-measurable”, in the strong form that it agrees μ_V-a.e. with a Borel function).

Combining Parts A, B and C proves MonotonicityFormula ∧ StationaryMonotonicityIdentity ∧ DensityExistsAE.
proof_key_steps: Radial field X_ρ = φ(|y−x|/ρ)(y−x): div_S X_ρ = nφ + r∂_rφ·(1 − |p_{S⊥}((y−x)/r)|²) (3.2).
Integrate: d/dρ(ρ^{-n}I) = ρ^{-n}J' − ρ^{-n-1}δV(X_ρ) with I = ∫φ dμ_V, J = ∫φ|p_{S⊥}|² dV, J' ≥ 0 (SimonGMT hasDerivAt_normalized_weightedCutoffMass, h ≡ 1).
With 2.6 (|δV(X)| ≤ ∫|X| d‖δV‖), layer cake and 3.1 extended to open balls: |δV(X_ρ)| ≤ (1+ε)Λρ I(ρ).
Integrating factor e^{Λ_ερ}: d/dρ(e^{Λ_ερ}ρ^{-n}I) ≥ ρ^{-n}J' ≥ 0; integrate on [σ,ρ], two-sided Ch. 4 3.5 bounds, let φ ↓ 1_{(−∞,1]}: additive form of 3.3.
Read off monotonicity, the density limit θ (monotone limit, e^{Λσ} → 1), θ ≤ e^{Λσ}densityRatio(σ), θ ≠ ∞; divide by ω_n.
Stationary case: δV(X_ρ) = 0 gives the annular identity (SimonGMT StationaryOn.stationaryMonotonicity with R ∈ (ρ,ρ0)); let σ ↓ 0 by monotone convergence, the centre contributing 0.
By 2.7 (first_variation), for μ_V-a.e. x ∈ U ∩ spt μ_V there are ρ0, Λ(x) with ball x ρ0 ⊆ U and ‖δV‖(B_ρ(x)) ≤ Λ(x)μ_V(B_ρ(x)), 0 < ρ < ρ0 (3.1).
At such x MonotonicityFormula gives a finite density θ_x.
x ↦ μ_V(B_ρ(x)) is Borel for each ρ (Tonelli for the σ-finite μ_V), so Θ(x) := liminf_k densityRatio n μ_V x (1/(k+1)) is Borel.
Where the density exists, Θ(x) equals it; hence Θ x ≠ ∞ ∧ HasDensity n μ_V x (Θ x) μ_V-a.e.

subproblem.title: Constancy Theorem 8.4.1 (corrected: M ∩ U connected)
subproblem.statement: Let V be a stationary n-varifold in open U ⊆ ℝ^N, M an n-dimensional C² submanifold of ℝ^N in Simon's sense (IsSimonSubmanifold 2 M), U ∩ spt μ_V ⊆ M, and M ∩ U preconnected (corrected hypothesis; the printed 'M connected' is false). Then there is θ0 ≥ 0 with V(A) = θ0 · H^n({x ∈ M ∩ U : (x, T_xM) ∈ A}) for every Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G(N,n), where T_xM is the plane equal to the classical tangent space classicalTangentSpace M x (velocities of C¹ curves in M through x). (Exactly ConstancyTheorem.)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 4.1 and its printed proof (pp. 213–214), with the documented erratum. ERRATUM (README; SimonGMT ConstancyDomainCounterexample.counterexample_constancy_printed_hypotheses): the printed hypothesis “M connected” is insufficient (U = ℝ ∖ {0}, M = ℝ, V = v((0,∞)) is stationary in U with spt ⊆ M but is not a constant multiple of v(M ∩ U)); the corrected hypothesis is that M ∩ U is (pre)connected, which is exactly what the last line of the printed proof uses. The conclusion V = θ0 v(M) is read in U, i.e. V = θ0 v(M ∩ U) with T_x M the classical tangent plane, and θ0 = 0 is allowed. Notation: μ = μ_V, H^n = μHE[n], G = Grassmannian N n, classicalTangentSpace M x = {γ'(0) : γ C¹ on (−1,1), γ((−1,1)) ⊆ M, γ(0) = x}.

Hypotheses: V is stationary in U (δV(X) = 0 for all X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N)); M is an n-dimensional C² submanifold of ℝ^N in Simon's sense (Ch. 2 §4: Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold (E := Euclidean n) 2 M — every point of M lies in an open W with a C², injective, relatively proper parametrization φ : D → W ∩ M, D ⊆ ℝ^n open, Dφ injective); U ∩ spt μ ⊆ M; M ∩ U is preconnected. Claim: ∃ θ0 ≥ 0 with V(A) = θ0 · H^n({x ∈ M ∩ U : (x, T_xM) ∈ A}) for all Borel A ⊆ ℝ^N × G, where T_xM ∈ G is the plane with plane = classicalTangentSpace M x.

0. Trivial case. If M ∩ U = ∅ then U ∩ spt μ = ∅, so μ(U) ≤ μ(U ∩ spt μ) + μ(ℝ^N ∖ spt μ) = 0 and μ(Uᶜ) = 0 (V.supported), hence V = 0 and θ0 = 0 works (both sides are 0). Assume M ∩ U ≠ ∅ below (this also covers n > N vacuously: then no injective Dφ exists, so M = ∅).

1. Classical tangent spaces. For x ∈ M and a local parametrization φ : D → W ∩ M with x = φ(a): classicalTangentSpace M x = range Dφ(a), an n-dimensional subspace, which we denote T_xM. (⊇) For v = Dφ(a)w take γ(t) = φ(a + g(t)w) with g smooth, bounded by r/|w| where B_r(a) ⊆ D, g(0) = 0, g'(0) = 1: γ is C¹ on (−1,1), lands in M, γ(0) = x, γ'(0) = v. (⊆) If γ is C¹ into M with γ(0) = x, then near t = 0, γ(t) ∈ W ∩ M = φ(D), and by the relative properness and the inverse function theorem (φ is a C² immersion and a homeomorphism onto W ∩ M) γ = φ ∘ β with β C¹ near 0, β(0) = a, so γ'(0) = Dφ(a)β'(0) ∈ range Dφ(a). Since a Grassmannian point is determined by its plane, T_xM ∈ G is well defined, and x ↦ T_xM is continuous on M (C¹ dependence of range Dφ).

2. Printed step (1)–(2): p_S(∇f) = 0 on spt V. Take any f ∈ C²_c(U) with f = 0 on M ∩ U (the printed “M ⊂ {x ∈ U : f(x) = 0}”, read in U). For such f, X := f∇f ∈ K(U;ℝ^N) and by 2.3, div_S(f∇f) = ∇^S f·∇f + f div_S∇f = |p_S(∇f)|² + f div_S ∇f; on spt μ ∩ U ⊆ M we have f = 0, so δV(f∇f) = ∫|p_S(∇f(x))|² dV(x,S) (V is carried by Gₙ(U ∩ spt μ)). Stationarity gives ∫|p_S(∇f(x))|² dV = 0, hence (by continuity of (x,S) ↦ |p_S(∇f(x))|²) p_S(∇f(x)) = 0 for all (x,S) ∈ spt V.

3. Printed step (3): S = T_xM on spt V. Let ξ ∈ M ∩ U. There are an open W ∋ ξ and C²_c(U) functions f_1,…,f_k (k = N − n) vanishing on M ∩ W such that ∇f_1(x),…,∇f_k(x) span (T_xM)^⊥ for every x ∈ M ∩ W (locally M ∩ W is the zero set of a C² submersion — straighten M by a C² chart around ξ and multiply the normal coordinates by a cutoff; one checks such W, f_j exist; SimonGMT ConstancyNormalCharts.exists_local_normal_defining_map, Chapter08/ConstancyNormalCharts.lean:90). Step 2 applied to each f_j gives p_S((T_xM)^⊥) = 0 for all (x,S) ∈ Gₙ(W) ∩ spt V, i.e. (T_xM)^⊥ ⊆ S^⊥; as dim S = dim T_xM = n, S = T_xM. Since ξ is arbitrary, V is carried by the graph {(x, T_xM) : x ∈ M ∩ U}:
 (4) ∫ f(x,S) dV(x,S) = ∫_{M∩U} f(x, T_xM) dμ(x) for f ∈ C_c(Gₙ(U)); equivalently V = μ.map(x ↦ (x, T_xM)) on Borel sets (μ is carried by M ∩ U).

4. Printed step (5): μ = θ H^n ⌞ (M ∩ U) with θ = Θ^n(μ,·). Since V is stationary in every open ball B°_ρ(x) ⊆ U, the monotonicity identity 3.4 (sibling monotonicity_density, second conjunct StationaryMonotonicityIdentity; the printed proof cites 3.3) shows θ(x) := Θ^n(μ, x) exists and is finite at every x ∈ U. Work on one chart sheet M ∩ W (W as in the definition of a Simon submanifold, W ∩ U ∩ M ≠ ∅); by Lindelöf countably many sheets cover M ∩ U. On a sheet, λ := H^n ⌞ (M ∩ W) is locally finite in W ∩ U (area formula for the C² chart) and Θ^n(λ, x) = 1 for every x ∈ M ∩ W (the chart is asymptotically linear at each point). (i) μ⌞(W∩U) ≪ λ: if Z ⊆ M ∩ W ∩ U and H^n(Z) = 0, write Z = ∪_k Z_k, Z_k := {x ∈ Z : θ(x) ≤ k}; for δ, η > 0 let Z_{k,δ} := {x ∈ Z_k : μ(B_ρ(x)) ≤ (k+η)ω_nρ^n for 0 < ρ ≤ δ} (Z_k = ∪_{δ} Z_{k,δ}); any cover of Z_{k,δ} by sets C_i of diameter d_i < δ meeting Z_{k,δ} at x_i satisfies Z_{k,δ} ⊆ ∪B_{d_i}(x_i), so μ(Z_{k,δ}) ≤ (k+η)Σω_n d_i^n = 2^n(k+η)Σω_n(d_i/2)^n, whence μ(Z_{k,δ}) ≤ 2^n(k+η)H^n_δ(Z_k) = 0; so μ(Z) = 0. Also μ is carried by M ∩ U (U ∩ spt μ ⊆ M). (ii) By the differentiation theorem (Ch. 1, 3.23–3.24; Radon measures on open subsets of ℝ^N have the symmetric Vitali property), μ⌞(W∩U) = (D_λ μ) λ with D_λμ(x) = lim μ(B_ρ(x))/λ(B_ρ(x)) = θ(x)/Θ^n(λ,x) = θ(x) for x ∈ M ∩ W ∩ U. Patching the sheets,
 (5) ∫ f(x,S) dV(x,S) = ∫_{M∩U} f(x, T_xM) θ(x) dH^n(x), f ∈ C_c(Gₙ(U)),
 i.e. V = v(M ∩ U, θ), θ locally H^n-integrable on M ∩ U.

5. θ is constant on M ∩ U (printed last paragraph). Fix a Simon chart φ : D → W ∩ M (D ⊆ ℝ^n open, φ C², Jφ := (det Dφᵀ Dφ)^{1/2} > 0 and C¹) with φ(D) ⊆ U, and put θ̃ := θ ∘ φ, which is locally L^n-integrable on D (area formula: ∫_{φ(K)} θ dH^n = ∫_K θ̃ Jφ dL^n < ∞ for compact K ⊆ D). For Y ∈ C¹_c(D;ℝ^n), the tangential field Z := (Dφ·Y) ∘ φ⁻¹ on M ∩ W extends to some X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N) with X = Z on M ∩ U (extend in the normal directions using a C² normal chart and a cutoff; M is C²), and div_M X ∘ φ = Jφ⁻¹ Σ_i ∂_i(Jφ Y_i) (divergence in local coordinates). subproblem.title: Theorem 8.3.7: semicontinuity of ‖δV‖ and of the density bound Θ^n ≥ 1 under varifold convergence
subproblem.statement: Let V_i, V be n-varifolds on open U ⊆ ℝ^N with V_i → V as Radon measures on Gₙ(U) (RadonConverges), each V_i of locally bounded first variation with liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(W) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and sets B_i ⊆ ℝ^N with Θ^n(μ_{V_i}, y) existing and ≥ 1 for all y ∈ U ∖ B_i and μ_{V_i}(B_i ∩ W) → 0 for every open W ⊂⊂ U. Then V has locally bounded first variation, ‖δV‖(W) ≤ liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(W) for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and for μ_V-a.e. y, Θ^n(μ_V, y) exists and is ≥ 1. (Exactly DensitySemicontinuity.)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 8, Theorem 3.7, Remark 3.8(1) and the printed proof of 3.7 (pp. 211–213). No erratum in the statement; details filled in: (a) the printed constant “c independent of i, j” is replaced by the liminf hypothesis exactly as stated (only liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(W̃) < ∞ is assumed), taken inside the liminf over q in step (3); (b) the sets B_i may be non-measurable, so μ_i(·) of them is outer measure (all estimates below are subadditivity/covering estimates, valid for outer measures); (c) the final “Θ^n(μ_V, y) ≥ 1” is a statement about the density, whose existence μ_V-a.e. comes from Lemma 3.6 (sibling monotonicity_density, third conjunct DensityExistsAE) applied to V. Notation: μ_i = μ_{V_i} = (Vi i).weight, μ = μ_V, ‖δV_i‖ = variationMeasure (Vi i), B_ρ(y) = closedBall y ρ, W ⊂⊂ U means IsRelCompactOpenIn W U (open, compact closure inside U).

Hypotheses: Vi → V (Varifold.RadonConverges, i.e. ∫ f dV_i → ∫ f dV for every f ∈ C_c(U × G)); each V_i has locally bounded first variation; liminf_i ‖δV_i‖(W) < ∞ for every W ⊂⊂ U; for every i and y ∈ U ∖ B_i, Θ^n(μ_i, y) exists and is ≥ 1; μ_i(B_i ∩ W) → 0 for every W ⊂⊂ U.

STEP 1 (first two conclusions; Remark 3.8(1), “a trivial consequence of the definitions”). For X ∈ K(U;ℝ^N), div_S X is a continuous function with compact support in U × G, so δV_i(X) → δV(X) (SimonGMT RadonConverges.firstVariation_tendsto). Hence for every set W, firstVariationNormOn V W ≤ liminf_i firstVariationNormOn V_i W (RadonConverges.firstVariationNormOn_le_liminf, VarifoldConvergence.lean). For open W ⊂⊂ U the sibling first_variation (2.5, IsFirstVariationMeasure) identifies variationMeasure V_i W = firstVariationNormOn V_i W; so the hypothesis gives liminf_i firstVariationNormOn V_i W < ∞, hence firstVariationNormOn V W < ∞ for all such W, i.e. V has locally bounded first variation (RadonConverges.hasLocallyBoundedFirstVariation), and then variationMeasure V W = firstVariationNormOn V W ≤ liminf_i variationMeasure V_i W for every open W ⊂⊂ U (RadonConverges.firstVariationRieszMeasure_le_liminf).

STEP 2 (portmanteau facts used below). Testing with functions of x alone (G is compact, so (x,S) ↦ f(x) is in C_c(U × G) for f ∈ C_c(U)), μ_i → μ as Radon measures on U. Consequently: (P1) μ(O) ≤ liminf_i μ_i(O) for open O ⊆ U; (P2) μ(K) ≥ limsup_i μ_i(K) for compact K ⊆ U (approximate 1_O from below and 1_K from above by functions in C_c(U), using inner/outer regularity of the Radon measure μ on U).

STEP 3 (the proof of 3.7). Fix W ⊂⊂ U and ρ0 > 0 with 2ρ0 < dist(closure W, ℝ^N ∖ U) (positive, closure W compact in U open; if U = ℝ^N simply take ρ0 := 1 — note Lean's infDist to ∅ is 0, so this case is treated separately); put W̃ := {x : dist(x, W) < ρ0}, which is open with compact closure inside U, so L := liminf_q ‖δV_q‖(W̃) < ∞. For y ∈ W and ρ < ρ0 we have B_ρ(y) ⊆ W̃ ⊆ U.
 (1) For i, j ≥ 1 let A_{i,j} be the set of y ∈ W ∖ B_i such that ‖δV_i‖(B_ρ(y)) ≤ j μ_i(B_ρ(y)) for all 0 < ρ < ρ0, and B_{i,j} := W ∖ A_{i,j}.
 (2) If x ∈ B_{i,j} then either x ∈ B_i ∩ W, or μ_i(B_σ(x)) < j^{-1}‖δV_i‖(B_σ(x)) for some σ ∈ (0, ρ0).
 Besicovitch. Let 𝔅 be the family of closed balls B_σ(x), x ∈ B_{i,j} ∖ B_i, σ ∈ (0,ρ0), satisfying (2). The centres form a bounded set, so by the Besicovitch Covering Lemma (Ch. 1 3.12) there are N = N(N_ambient) countable subfamilies 𝔅_1,…,𝔅_N ⊆ 𝔅, each pairwise disjoint, whose union covers B_{i,j} ∖ B_i. Summing (2) over them (all balls lie in W̃): μ_i(B_{i,j}) ≤ μ_i(B_{i,j} ∖ B_i) + μ_i(B_i ∩ W) ≤ N j^{-1} ‖δV_i‖(W̃) + μ_i(B_i ∩ W) (outer measure, countable subadditivity).
 (3) For i, j ≥ 1 put O_{i,j} := interior(∩_{ℓ≥i} B_{ℓ,j}) (open, ⊆ W). For q ≥ i, O_{i,j} ⊆ B_{q,j}, so by (P1) and the previous estimate μ(O_{i,j}) ≤ liminf_q μ_q(O_{i,j}) ≤ liminf_q (N j^{-1}‖δV_q‖(W̃) + μ_q(B_q ∩ W)) ≤ N j^{-1} L, using μ_q(B_q ∩ W) → 0 (liminf(a_q + b_q) ≤ liminf a_q + limsup b_q). Write c := N L.
 (4) Lower density outside the bad set. Fix j and suppose x ∈ W ∖ ∪_i O_{i,j}. Then for each i we can pick y_i ∈ W ∩ B°_{1/i}(x) with y_i ∉ ∩_{q≥i}B_{q,j} (W ∩ B°_{1/i}(x) is an open neighbourhood of x and x is not an interior point of ∩_{q≥i}B_{q,j}), hence q_i ≥ i with y_i ∉ B_{q_i,j}, i.e. y_i ∈ A_{q_i,j}: y_i ∈ W ∖ B_{q_i} and ‖δV_{q_i}‖(B_ρ(y_i)) ≤ j μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(y_i)) for 0 < ρ < ρ0. Since ball y_i ρ0 ⊆ U, the monotonicity formula 3.3 (sibling monotonicity_density, first conjunct MonotonicityFormula with Λ = j) gives Θ^n(μ_{q_i}, y_i) ≤ e^{jρ} ω_n^{-1} ρ^{-n} μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(y_i)) (0 < ρ < ρ0), and Θ^n(μ_{q_i}, y_i) ≥ 1 because y_i ∈ U ∖ B_{q_i} (uniqueness of limits identifies the two densities). So μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(y_i)) ≥ e^{-jρ} ω_n ρ^n for 0 < ρ < ρ0. Fix 0 < ρ < ρ0; for i large, |y_i − x| < ρ and B_{ρ−|y_i−x|}(y_i) ⊆ B_ρ(x), so by (P2) (B_ρ(x) compact ⊆ U) μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_i μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(x)) ≥ limsup_i e^{-jρ}ω_n(ρ − |y_i − x|)^n = e^{-jρ} ω_n ρ^n. Hence the lower density liminf_{ρ↓0} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρ^n) ≥ 1 for every x ∈ W ∖ ∪_i O_{i,j}, for some j; i.e. it is ≥ 1 for every x ∈ W ∖ E_W, E_W := ∩_{j≥1} ∪_{i≥1} O_{i,j}.
 (5) μ(E_W) = 0: O_{i,j} increases with i, so μ(E_W) ≤ μ(∪_i O_{i,j}) = lim_i μ(O_{i,j}) ≤ c j^{-1} for every j.

STEP 4 (conclusion). By Step 1, V has locally bounded first variation, so by the sibling monotonicity_density (third conjunct, DensityExistsAE), Θ^n(μ, y) exists (and is finite) for μ-a.e. y. Cover U by countably many W ⊂⊂ U (e.g. W_m = {x ∈ U : |x| < m, dist(x, ℝ^N∖U) > 1/m}); off the μ-null set ∪_m E_{W_m} ∪ {density fails to exist} ∪ Uᶜ, the density exists and is ≥ its lower density ≥ 1. Hence ∀ᵐ y ∂μ_V, ∃ θ, HasDensity n μ_V y θ ∧ 1 ≤ θ. Together with Step 1 this is DensitySemicontinuity.
proof_key_steps: Remark 3.8(1): δV_i(X) → δV(X), so firstVariationNormOn is lower semicontinuous; with 2.5 this gives LBFV of V and ‖δV‖(W) ≤ liminf ‖δV_i‖(W) (SimonGMT VarifoldConvergence).
Portmanteau for weights: μ(O) ≤ liminf μ_i(O) (O open), μ(K) ≥ limsup μ_i(K) (K compact).
Printed (1)–(2): bad sets B_{i,j}; Besicovitch gives μ_i(B_{i,j}) ≤ N j^{-1}‖δV_i‖(W̃) + μ_i(B_i ∩ W).
Printed (3): μ(interior ∩_{ℓ≥i}B_{ℓ,j}) ≤ N j^{-1} liminf_q ‖δV_q‖(W̃) =: c/j.
Printed (4): outside ∪_i interior(∩_{ℓ≥i}B_{ℓ,j}), points y_i → x with 3.1 at y_i (Λ = j) and Θ ≥ 1 give μ_{q_i}(B_ρ(y_i)) ≥ e^{-jρ}ω_nρ^n by 3.3, hence lower density ≥ 1 at x.
Printed (5): the exceptional set has μ-measure ≤ c/j for all j, so is null; Lemma 3.6 for V gives existence of Θ^n(μ_V,·) a.e., hence Θ ≥ 1 a.e.

audit.reason: The proof uses the actual liminf hypothesis without assuming uniform variation bounds. The Besicovitch estimates, portmanteau passage and null exceptional set establish the density lower bound; the declared predecessors supply density existence and variation lower semicontinuity.
